title: Chicken Shawarma Wrap with Creamy Garlic Sauce
summary: Thin-sliced chicken thigh marinated for two days in a freshly ground spice and citrus blend, seared in tallow and rolled in saj with an egg-white garlic sauce, shatta, pomegranate molasses, pickles and crisp chicken skin.
notes: Video: 'The Best Shawarma At Home' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Made with the chef of Miya Miya Shawarma (Los Angeles). Written recipe: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/the-best-homemade-chicken-shawarma-sandwich-recipe (serves 10; prep 1 hour plus a 24-48 hour marinade, cook 30 min). All spice, marinade and garlic-sauce amounts are stated in the video and match the written recipe. The written recipe puts about 3/4 of the marinade on the meat and 1/4 on the skins, with nothing drained off, and both are eaten, so the whole marinade counts (a blended marinade that stays on the meat; judgment call, since it is citrus-heavy). The garlic sauce is spread generously inside and dolloped on top, so the whole batch counts (house rule: sauce on the dish), The oil is the one part made in excess: house rule 10 says to count a stated share, and they state it ('we use like about 90% of the oil'), so the oil counts at 0.9 x 360 mL = 324 mL; the rest of the sauce (egg whites, garlic, salt, lemon) is fully used and counts in full. Our estimates, because neither the video nor the page gives amounts used: 10 flatbreads at 60 g, shatta 2 tsp and pomegranate molasses 1 1/2 tsp per wrap, drained pickles 280 g (60% of a 16 oz jar), beef tallow 2 Tbsp for the chicken and 1 tsp per wrap, nutmeg 1/8 tsp, zest 1 Tbsp per lemon or orange, orange juice 86 g (USDA). Ranges: garlic-sauce oil 1-1 1/2 cups (see above). Not counted: cooking spray for the alternative oven method for the skins; the pan juices the wrap is dipped in (already in the chicken). Proxies: Aleppo pepper uses paprika; shatta uses a red chili paste record; saj uses white pita; Greek yogurt uses plain whole-milk yogurt; the neutral oil (refined avocado or light olive oil) uses canola. The chicken is counted as raw skin-on thigh because the skin is eaten as crisps; trimmed fat and fat rendered from the skins make this a slight overestimate.

steps.text: Grind the whole spices (white pepper, coriander, cardamom, cloves, cumin, cinnamon) fresh in a spice grinder, then mix with the curry powder, bouillon, thyme, oregano, Aleppo pepper, a little nutmeg and the salt.

Blend the zest of 2 lemons and the juice of 5, the zest and juice of the orange, shatta, yogurt, vinegar, garlic and the spice mix on high for about a minute, until smooth. Taste it: it should be sharp and well salted.

Pull the skin off the thighs and keep it. Trim away all visible fat. Freeze the meat about 30 minutes, then slice it into very thin strips, about 1/4 inch or thinner, some thinner than others for crispier bits.
Toss the chicken with most of the marinade and coat the skins with the rest. Cover and refrigerate at least 24 hours, ideally 48.

Chicken crisps: press the marinated skins dry and lay them flat in a cold 12-inch nonstick pan over medium-low, weighed down with a press or another pan, about 10 minutes until crisp. Or bake them flat between sprayed, parchment-lined sheet trays at about 370°F for 10-15 minutes.
Sear the chicken in batches in a pan lightly coated with beef tallow over medium-high, about 1-1 1/2 minutes per side, until browned. Hold on a tray, tented with foil, without overcooking.
Garlic sauce: blend the egg whites with the garlic on high until frothy and completely smooth.
Move it to a food processor, add the salt and lemon juice, and with the machine running pour in the oil in the thinnest stream until thick and creamy (about 90% of the oil was used).
Cut the baby dill pickles into thin, even matchsticks.

Lay out a saj or shrak (or pita). Spread generously with garlic sauce, add a light layer of shatta and a drizzle of pomegranate molasses, cover with pickles, pile on the chicken and crumble chicken skin over it, not too fine.
Roll it up tightly, dip it lightly in the chicken pan juices, and sear in a large pan with a little beef tallow until golden, 1-2 minutes per side.
Wrap in parchment or foil and top each with a dollop of garlic sauce, a piece of chicken skin and a light drizzle of pomegranate molasses.
